purpose: Validate integrated native-boundary acceptance on one independent Linux runner; preserve every trial and original startup verdict.
scope: Six direct WebRTC trials with identical images in 1s/3s/3s/1s/1s/3s down-hold order. No tunnel, TURN, MediaMTX, authentication or physical camera is exercised.

All six trials pass media, playback, automatic source-format, target recovery and required native-boundary gates. All twelve native boundaries are valid and all steady capacity/recovery freeze increments are zero. Baseline frozen time is also zero in all six trials.

All three public-default 3s trials pass all 23 gates. Trials one, four and five fail only exact first-presentation measurement: their first callbacks report two submitted frames. Exact durations remain unknown and failed verdicts remain unchanged. These trials precede the visible-observation collector and cannot establish its visibility evidence.

Transition frozen time is 1.819–1.930s at 1s down-hold and 1.905–2.052s at 3s down-hold. This finite sample does not justify changing the public 3s default or establish target hardware performance. Historical failed trials remain failed.
